title: Exponential-polynomial bound for exponentials
statement: For all $c,e\in\mathbb{N}$, the function $n\mapsto c\,2^{n^e}$ is exponential-polynomial: there exist $K,k\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $c\,2^{n^e}\le 2^{K(n+1)^k}$ for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$.
replaced:
For all constants $c, e \in \mathbb{N}$, the function $n \mapsto c \cdot 2^{n^e}$ is
exponential-polynomial: there exist constants $K, k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that
$c \cdot 2^{n^e} \le 2^{K(n+1)^k}$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
